scenes.narration_excerpt: You wanted to be a pirate. Gold, freedom, a magnificent coat. Instead, you are holding a bucket below deck while somebody above you asks whether you have finished cleaning the ship's most disgusting corner.
scenes.authored_action: Tom kneels beside the shallow bilge with the plain wooden bucket and grimaces upward at a voice through the hatch.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Opening flash-forward to routine, not whole voyage chronology. Same bucket persists033/085; no sewage gore.

scenes.narration_excerpt: The magnificent coat belongs to someone else. Your shirt has a patch, your breakfast could damage a tooth, and the bucket is yours. Congratulations: you have successfully escaped ordinary employment into unusually dangerous employment.
scenes.authored_action: Tom holds bucket by a deck corner while captain in modestly better coat passes; close patched sleeve and ordinary food bowl visible.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Tom retains navy waistcoat, cream patched shirt, dark trousers; never becomes ornate captain.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Imagine you are Tom, an adult sailor in the Caribbean around seventeen fifteen. Your crew and personal journey are fictional, but the problems come from the history of seafaring during piracy's so-called golden age.
scenes.authored_action: Tom stands by the Caribbean quay with his small cloth bundle, wooden vessels and low colonial houses behind.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Explicit new story start ashore before enlistment; no giant fort/castle fantasy or modern ship.

scenes.narration_excerpt: That age was golden mainly for later storytellers. Royal Museums Greenwich places the familiar Atlantic boom between the sixteen eighties and seventeen twenties. It was not a comfortable retirement program with optional sword fights.
scenes.authored_action: Tom watches a wealthy shipowner's cargo pass him while staying beside his humble belongings.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Atlantic c1715 context; no time-travel famous-pirate portraits or generated date text.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You begin ashore, carrying your belongings in a small bundle. You know ships, hard work, and disappointing wages.
scenes.authored_action: Tom shoulders the single bundle and approaches waterfront work.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Same fixed harbor buildings; bundle exact cloth/color aftercarry.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Work at sea could be harsh. The museum describes poor pay and heavy labor in merchant shipping, alongside severe naval discipline. Piracy promised some sailors another way out. A promise is not a guarantee.
scenes.authored_action: Tom pauses beside exhausted seamen hauling normal commercial goods; crewmate gestures to the difficult work.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Merchant-work illustrative group distinct from protagonist; no flogging scene or branded company insignia.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Nor did every person aboard a pirate vessel join enthusiastically. Captured crews might supply recruits, and coercion complicated the picture. Your imagined choice is voluntary. That does not make everybody else's experience the same.
scenes.authored_action: Tom watches a worried captured-sailor illustrative aside near a working vessel while he remains free to choose.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Contextual historical aside, not implication Tom personally freed/coercedsomeone; restrained adult extras.

scenes.narration_excerpt: And these were criminals taking other people's property, sometimes their freedom or lives. Understanding the appeal does not turn the victims into scenery. The adventure you are considering has someone else's fear inside it.
scenes.authored_action: Tom notices a civilian clutching a partly emptied cargo container, concern rather than heroic cheering.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Victim perspective, no crime instructions, no violent theft contact; not identical face clone of main Tom.

scenes.narration_excerpt: At a waterfront tavern, an experienced sailor describes a crew preparing to sail. There could be a share of captured wealth, he says. You notice he describes the wealth more carefully than the work.
scenes.authored_action: Crewwmate leans across a rough tavern table while Tom listens to promises of a share.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Plain mugs not modern bottles/labels; same tavern chairs/windows fixed for laterreturn069–070.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You ask about the vessel. It is a modest wooden sloop, not a floating palace with five decks of cannons. Pirates used different ships. Your fictional crew's boat is small enough to feel everybody's elbows.
scenes.authored_action: Tom looks closely at the modest single-mast sloop moored at the known quay.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Same DECK vessel anchored; no multideck galleon, ornatecaptainluxury or Norwegianlongship.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Down at the quay, the quartermaster meets you. In some pirate crews, this officer helped manage supplies and represent crew interests. The title did not mean you were about to receive hotel service.
scenes.authored_action: Quartermaster meets Tom at the gangway, stores bundle at his feet.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Quartermaster distinct muted attire, not modern naval officer; maincastrole consistent.

scenes.narration_excerpt: He asks what you can do. You know the basic work of a sailor and can help keep a vessel running.
scenes.authored_action: Tom demonstrates working knowledge by coiling an existing rope while quartermaster observes.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Ordinary competence not piracy technique; fixedmast/hatch/tiller/cannons geometry.

scenes.narration_excerpt: The captain stands nearby, looking considerably more important than you. Nobody hands you a feathered hat and instantly promotes your opinions into policy.
scenes.authored_action: Captain looks over work near aft tiller while Tom waits with plain bundle.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Captaindifferentwardrobe, Tom no hat/epaulets; no fantasy crown or modernwheel.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You inspect the deck, mast, sail, and rigging. The ropes are not decorative lines surrounding an adventure. They are equipment that somebody must understand, handle, maintain, and replace before trouble makes the lesson memorable.
scenes.authored_action: Tom checks existing line and turns to the main mast while crewmate points to sail seam.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Rig fixed to approved master, all lines physically connected; no generic square-riggedfrigate substitution.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Below deck, the space is cramped. There are supplies, personal belongings, and the unmistakable smell of a working ship.
scenes.authored_action: Tom stoops through the hatch and looks at cramped stores and sleeping spaces.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Hatch/headroom/mast supports mirror approved DECK; hull cannot enlarge between shots.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You place your bundle beside the sleeping area. Another sailor moves it slightly because it is in his way. Your first territorial conflict involves approximately enough space to put down one tired human.
scenes.authored_action: Tom places bundle beside a sleeping spot; crewmate shifts it slightly away from his own blanket.
scenes.continuity_requirements: One bundle, one explainable relocation; no luxurious bunks or duplicateToms.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Then the crew's rules are explained. Many pirate companies had agreements, often called articles, covering conduct and the division of proceeds. They were practical arrangements, not the identical universal code from every movie.
scenes.authored_action: Quartermaster explains plain crew articles on a sheet as Tom listens, captain nearby.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Articles no readable generatedtext/fakefixedrates; document plausibleashore/crewmeetingnotmodernlegalcontract.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Some surviving accounts include compensation for injury and rules about disputes or gambling. The details differed. Your imagined crew has its own bargain; we are not going to invent a standard pirate benefits package.
scenes.authored_action: Quartermaster gestures to a simple bandaged hand of crewmate while discussing rules; Tom listens thoughtfully.
scenes.continuity_requirements: No amputation/gore, no numeric universal compensation; existingpaperstayssameobject.

scenes.narration_excerpt: The promise of a share can sound better than a poor wage. But a share of disappointing proceeds remains disappointing. If the expedition earns little, arithmetic will not create a magnificent fortune out of enthusiasm.
scenes.authored_action: Tom holds an almost empty personal purse beside humble belongings and looks toward stored goods.
scenes.continuity_requirements: No invented exact earnings or payment table; money expectations conceptual.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Captains could be chosen by crews, and some could be removed. It does not mean every vessel was equally democratic, gentle, or welcoming to everybody.
scenes.authored_action: Small crew gathering: Tom and crewmate raise a hand while captain stands listening.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Illustrates some crew decisionpractices, not guaranteedallpiratedemocracy; no modern ballotboxes.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Authority still mattered, especially during dangerous encounters. You might have a voice in a decision without being free to wander away from your assigned work. Freedom apparently comes with a rope that needs handling.
scenes.authored_action: Captain gestures toward necessary work and Tom picks up the waiting line.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Voice in decision doesnoterasejobs; same rope fixed orientation.

scenes.narration_excerpt: And an agreement cannot remove prejudice, violence, or unequal power. Pirates included people from different backgrounds, but the romantic idea of universal equality does not survive a close look at the wider history.
scenes.authored_action: Tom notices quartermaster giving an order while an excluded adult captive stands separately under concern.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Humanrightsquestion, no implicationtotalequality or mainactor clone captives.

scenes.narration_excerpt: The quartermaster checks provisions while you carry a water container aboard. Water matters before treasure does. A ship can go surprisingly far on ambition, provided somebody has remembered the food and drink as well.
scenes.authored_action: Tom carries a filled wooden water container to gangway as quartermaster checks supplies.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Container needs practicalsize/dryhandledgrip, no modernwaterbottle; fixedpropsstow nextscene.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You help stow sacks and barrels securely. There is only so much room. Extra supplies compete with equipment, crew, and any cargo you hope to take later.
scenes.authored_action: Tom and crewmate stow a sack and secure wooden containers beside the centralmast support.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Leaveaccess passage free, barrelpositiontrackedafterloading; no cannonobstruction of hatch.

scenes.narration_excerpt: A sailor shows you the tools used for ordinary repairs. Wood, rope, cloth, and iron fittings all wear. You have joined an armed crew, but much of your success will depend on maintenance.
scenes.authored_action: Crewwmate shows Tom a needle, spare rope and simple woodworking tool laid on a cloth.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Maintenanceobjectsnotweaponconstruction; toolsplain17th–18thcentury notelectricdrill.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Weapons are present too. They are dangerous objects in crowded hands, not a guarantee that their owner will win. You would prefer every confrontation to end before anybody discovers how vulnerable you actually are.
scenes.authored_action: Tom checks the safely stowed small ship guns and sheathed arms while captain watches calm.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Exactlyapproved2smallcannons, noaiming/loading/firingtutorial or extraweaponsin hands.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You have simple working clothes and practical gear. A successful captain might display expensive finery. The new sailor hauling a sack does not suddenly own that captain's wardrobe, reputation, or much better-looking boots.
scenes.authored_action: Tom shoulders a supply sack past captain's better coat and practical boots.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Poornewrecruitcostumeconsistent; captain notluxuryaristocrat fromlatercentury.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Finally, you leave the harbor. Houses shrink behind you, the shore slips away, and for a moment the horizon looks wonderfully open.
scenes.authored_action: From aft, Tom watches lowharborhouses recede as captain holds tiller.

scenes.narration_excerpt: The first instruction is not to admire the horizon. You handle a line while another sailor works beside you. The vessel needs coordination. It is not impressed by your private discovery that the ocean is large.
scenes.authored_action: Tom tends a working line while crewmate assists near the mast.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Mainmast/hatch/cannons unchanged; not merelynewzoom but activeequipmenthandling.

scenes.narration_excerpt: When the wind shifts, the work changes with it. Sail handling, steering, lookout duties, and repairs remain necessary. A pirate ship is still a ship, which is a detail the recruitment speech underemphasized.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You climb carefully to work where you are needed. The deck moves below, rope presses into your hands, and the height becomes much more interesting now that there is no modern safety briefing.

scenes.authored_action: Tom scrubs a damp deck section with simple brush and water bucket.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Same opening bucket, cannons/hatchlockedpositions, wetdecknotunrelatedmodernboat.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You start dreaming about fresh fruit, then about a quiet bed. After a while, the fantasy of gold has acquired several extremely ordinary conditions.

scenes.continuity_requirements: Freshfruithunger throughbodylanguage, no thoughtbubbleor metaphoricfloatingbed required.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Over prolonged periods without enough fresh, suitable food, another danger could appear: scurvy. Royal Museums Greenwich explains that it results from a sustained lack of vitamin C. It was a serious threat to sailors.
scenes.authored_action: Crewwmate sits fatigued near depleted provisions while Tom notices concern.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Scurvyis risk conceptualaside, not definitiveinstantdiagnosis of Tom; days/weeksillustrativetimeadvance.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Weakness and painful symptoms could make work harder before the illness became fatal. This was not something every pirate developed after missing one orange. Diet and time mattered, and supplies differed between voyages.
scenes.authored_action: Tom offers crewmate a small foodportion as the latter looks tired and holds an achy hand.
scenes.continuity_requirements: No bleedinggums/fallingteeth/amputation; balancedscurvy framing, no inventeduniversalillness.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Your crew does not understand vitamins in the modern sense. Fresh food can help, but a reliable scientific solution is not sitting in your medical cupboard. A beautifully brave attitude does not replace missing nutrition.
scenes.authored_action: Tom examines a simple medicinebox while quartermaster checks scarce freshsupplies nearby.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Empty/no modernvitaminpills/antibiotics; no fraudulentbottlelabels or pseudo cure recipe.

scenes.narration_excerpt: Nor does rum. Pirates were not permanently drunk, whatever the costume suggests. Drink might offer pleasure, but handling equipment on a moving vessel while helplessly intoxicated introduces a very practical disagreement with gravity.
scenes.authored_action: Tom sets a plain drinkingcup aside and steadies himself near workingrope while crewmate continues duty.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Rum notshownasmedicalcure; no intoxicatedweaponuse, nocostumeparrot.

scenes.narration_excerpt: At night, you settle into your sleeping space. Someone nearby snores; another man shifts; the ship creaks. You have paid for your escape from ordinary life with exceptionally close access to other people's noises.
scenes.authored_action: Tom lies in established sleeping space while crewmate shifts nearby, dim lantern light.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Samehatch/stores, secureperiodlamp not electriclight; no cabinfurniture magicallyadded.

scenes.narration_excerpt: You are woken for your next duty. Rest depends on the needs of the ship, not simply on when you feel finished. The sea has never agreed to respect your preferred working hours.
scenes.authored_action: Crewwmate wakes Tom with a lightshouldertap; Tom reaches for his foldedclothing.
scenes.continuity_requirements: Night→predawn explicit, sameplainclothes; no suddenmainactor costume change.

scenes.narration_excerpt: A darker sky brings more work. The crew adjusts sail and secures what must stay in place. You watch rain sweep across the deck and understand that threatening strangers is irrelevant to controlling weather.

scenes.continuity_requirements: Reviewedstormvariantofsamevessel; modest roughweather not monsterwave.

scenes.narration_excerpt: The popular image focuses on spectacular battles. Intimidation could sometimes produce surrender without one. That did not make piracy harmless: the threat itself could take property and control away from people facing it.
